The core innovation lies in combining kernel regression with transformer-style attention through a learned kernel bias. Each KRBlock performs Nadaraya-Watson regression, where kernel similarity determines influence weights. This allows for translation invariance and efficient computation. The kernel attention bias extends this by incorporating index set information (e.g., time, location) into the attention mechanism via RBF kernels. This enables temporal causality and spatial locality, critical for GSE’s weekly predictions. Deep Kernel Attention replaces softmax with layer normalization, reducing computational overhead while maintaining expressiveness. These primitives form a scalable neural process framework that adapts to few-shot learning scenarios, particularly suited for GSI’s Bayesian inference and GSE’s situational reasoning. Failure modes include breakdown under non-stationary index sets or insufficient kernel capacity. The method assumes conditional independence of test points given context, which may limit joint distribution modeling in complex betting scenarios.
